problem:
Problem description
- There is an investor with initial capital $$B$$ and a finite planning horizon of $$H$$ periods.
- There are $$N$$ investment alternatives indexed by $$i \in \mathcal{I}$$, where each alternative has a guaranteed payoff structure.
- Investment alternative $$i$$ requires a holding period of $$\tau_i$$ periods and produces a guaranteed terminal cash amount of $$\gamma_i$$ per unit of capital invested.
- The decision is to allocate the available capital across the feasible investment alternatives and feasible start periods so that the terminal wealth at the end of period $$H$$ is maximized.
- The investment amount committed to a choice remains unavailable until that investment matures.
- An investment may only be started if it can still mature within the planning horizon.
- Capital is allocated linearly and proportionally across the available alternatives.
- The investment plan must respect the available budget and any timing restrictions implied by the holding periods.
- If idle cash is allowed, uninvested capital may remain as cash; otherwise, the full budget must be committed according to the plan.
- The planning goal is to maximize the total wealth available at the end of the horizon.
- A solution is represented by:
  - $$x_{t,i}$$: the amount of capital invested in alternative $$i$$ when started at period $$t$$
  - $$c_t$$: the cash balance carried into period $$t$$, if a cash state is included
  - $$W_H$$: the terminal wealth at the end of period $$H$$
  - The complete solution specifies all feasible investment amounts and the resulting maximum terminal wealth

Input Format
{
  "budget": "Initial available capital $$B$$",
  "horizon_periods": "Planning horizon length $$H$$",
  "investment_options": [
    {
      "option_id": "Investment alternative index $$i$$",
      "holding_period": "Holding duration $$\tau_i$$",
      "guaranteed_payoff_per_unit": "Guaranteed terminal payoff $$\gamma_i$$ per unit invested"
    }
  ],
  "feasible_start_periods": "Optional set of valid start periods $$\mathcal{T}_i$$ for each option, meaning the periods in which the option can be initiated and still mature by $$H$$",
  "cash_allowed": "Boolean indicator of whether unused capital may remain as cash"
}

Output Format
{
  "investment_plan": [
    {
      "start_period": "Start period index $$t$$",
      "option_id": "Investment option index $$i$$",
      "amount_invested": "Optimal investment amount $$x_{t,i}$$"
    }
  ],
  "terminal_wealth": "Maximum wealth at the end of period $$H$$, denoted $$W_H$$"
}

Example(s)

Input 1
{
  "budget": 100000,
  "horizon_periods": 3,
  "investment_options": [
    {
      "option_id": 1,
      "holding_period": 1,
      "guaranteed_payoff_per_unit": 0.7
    },
    {
      "option_id": 2,
      "holding_period": 2,
      "guaranteed_payoff_per_unit": 2
    }
  ],
  "cash_allowed": false
}

parameters.name: horizon_periods
parameters.description: Number of planning periods in the horizon

parameters.name: holding_periods
parameters.description: Holding period of each investment option

parameters.name: guaranteed_payoffs
parameters.description: Guaranteed terminal payoff per unit invested for each option

parameters.name: feasible_start_periods
parameters.description: Feasible start periods for each investment option, if provided

variables.name: investment_amounts
variables.description: Amount of capital invested in option i when started at period t

variables.name: cash_balance
variables.description: Cash balance carried into each period, if cash state is included

variables.name: terminal_wealth
variables.description: Terminal wealth at the end of the planning horizon

constraints.name: budget_nonnegativity
constraints.description: Initial capital budget must be nonnegative

constraints.name: horizon_positivity
constraints.description: Planning horizon must be a positive integer

constraints.name: option_count_positivity
constraints.description: Number of investment options must be a positive integer

constraints.name: holding_period_positivity
constraints.description: Each investment option must have a positive holding period

constraints.name: payoff_nonnegativity
constraints.description: Guaranteed terminal payoff per unit must be nonnegative for each option

constraints.name: cash_nonnegativity
constraints.description: Cash balances must be nonnegative when cash is modeled

constraints.name: maturity_feasible_start_periods
constraints.description: An investment may start only in periods that allow maturity within the horizon

constraints.name: option_specific_start_set_restriction
constraints.description: If feasible start periods are provided for an option, investment is allowed only in those periods

constraints.name: initial_budget_allocation
constraints.description: The initial budget can be split between cash and investments started in period 0

constraints.name: cash_flow_recursion
constraints.description: Cash carried to the next period equals current cash minus new investments plus matured proceeds from investments started earlier
constraints.formula: c_{t+1} = c_t - \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} x_{t,i} + \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}:\ t-\tau_i \geq 0} \gamma_i x_{t-\tau_i,i} \quad \forall t \in \{0,\dots,H-1\}

constraints.name: terminal_wealth_definition
constraints.description: Terminal wealth is equal to the final cash balance at the end of the horizon

objectives.name: terminal_wealth_maximization
objectives.description: Maximize terminal wealth at the end of the planning horizon

final_objective.description: Maximize terminal wealth at the end of the planning horizon using the single given objective.
